name: PhishingAttack
description: A case template for handling suspected or confirmed phishing incidents, including validation, analysis, scoping, containment, remediation, communications, and post-incident improvement.
author: Zachary Carter
summary:
## Incident Report — [CASE TITLE]

## Executive Summary

**[Provide a high-level, non-technical summary suitable for senior leadership. Describe the nature of the phishing campaign (e.g. credential harvesting, malware delivery, BEC-enabling), how it was identified, the number of recipients affected, whether any users interacted with the content, and the current containment and remediation status. Typically two to four paragraphs.]**

## Scope of Investigation

**[Define the boundaries of this investigation — which mailboxes, environments, and time periods were searched, what was explicitly excluded, and any limitations on message trace data, log availability, or endpoint telemetry that constrained findings.]**

## Campaign Analysis

**[Summarise the technical characteristics of the phishing campaign. Complete each subsection with observed data. Remove sections where no activity was observed and note the absence explicitly.]**

### Campaign Classification

**Phishing subtype:** <!-- Credential harvesting / Malware delivery / BEC-enabling / Callback / QR phishing / Spearphishing / Whaling / Other -->

**ATT&CK Technique(s):** <!-- e.g. T1566.001 Spearphishing Attachment, T1566.002 Spearphishing Link, T1598 Phishing for Information -->

**Suspected intent:** <!-- Credential theft / Malware deployment / Financial fraud / Data access / Reconnaissance -->

**[Describe the lure theme, impersonated entity, social engineering technique, and any personalisation or targeting observed. Note whether this appears to be an isolated message or part of a broader campaign.]**

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| Impersonated entity | |
| Lure theme / pretext | |
| Urgency or pressure cues | Yes / No |
| Personalisation observed | Yes / No |
| Isolated or campaign | Isolated / Suspected campaign / Confirmed campaign |

### Sender and Delivery

**[Summarise the sender identity, authentication results, delivery path, and any spoofing or impersonation technique used. Note whether the email bypassed security controls and why.]**

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| Sending address | |
| Sending IP | |
| SPF / DKIM / DMARC | Pass / Fail — |
| Spoofing technique | Display name / Lookalike domain / Compromised account / None |
| Delivered to | Inbox / Junk / Quarantine |
| Security control bypass | Yes / No — reason: |

### URLs and Infrastructure

**[Describe embedded URLs, redirect chains, landing page behavior, and hosting infrastructure. Note any use of URL shorteners, legitimate service abuse, or open redirect exploitation.]**

**Malicious URLs confirmed:** <!-- Yes / No / Under investigation -->

| URL / Domain | Role | Verdict | Actioned? |
|-------------|------|---------|----------|
| | Landing page / Redirect / C2 / Credential harvest | Malicious / Suspicious / Unknown | Blocked / Pending |

### Attachments and Payload

**[Describe any attachments, their behavior, and whether a payload was delivered or executed. Omit if no attachment was present.]**

**Malicious attachment confirmed:** <!-- Yes / No / Not applicable -->

| Filename | SHA-256 | Type | Behavior | Verdict |
|----------|---------|------|----------|--------|
| | | | Macro / Dropper / RAT / Stealer / Exploit / Other | Malicious / Suspicious / Unknown |

---

## Scope and User Impact

**[Summarise the campaign reach, user interactions, account compromise status, and any host impact. Reference the Scope and Impact notes for full detail.]**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Total recipients** | |
| **Confirmed interactions** | <!-- e.g. 3 clicked, 1 submitted credentials --> |
| **Confirmed compromised accounts** | |
| **Confirmed compromised hosts** | |
| **BEC concern identified** | <!-- Yes / No / Unknown --> |

### User Interactions

| User | Interaction | Date/Time (UTC) | Host | Compromise Status |
|------|------------|----------------|------|------------------|
| | Opened / Link clicked / Credential submitted / Attachment opened / Macro enabled / MFA approved | | | Confirmed / Suspected / Not compromised |

---

## IOC Summary

**[List validated indicators of compromise extracted from this campaign. Full IOC records are tracked in the case IOC objects.]**

| Indicator | Type | Context | Confidence |
|-----------|------|---------|------------|
| | Sender address / Sending IP / URL / Domain / File hash | | High / Medium / Low |

---

## Remediation & Recommendations

### Immediate Actions

| # | Action | Owner | Priority | Due |
|---|--------|-------|----------|-----|
| 1 | Remove or quarantine all matching messages from affected mailboxes | | Critical | |
| 2 | Block malicious sender addresses, domains, URLs, and file hashes across email and proxy controls | | Critical | |
| 3 | Reset credentials and revoke sessions for all users who submitted credentials or show compromise indicators | | Critical | |
| 4 | Review and remove any malicious inbox rules on affected accounts | | Critical | |
| 5 | Isolate and triage any hosts where attachments were opened or payloads executed | | Critical | |
| 6 | Notify affected recipients with clear guidance on required actions | | High | |

### Strategic Improvements

| # | Recommendation | Category | Priority |
|---|---------------|----------|----------|
| 1 | Enforce phishing-resistant MFA across all accounts to limit credential theft impact | Identity | High |
| 2 | Tighten DMARC policy to p=reject and review anti-impersonation controls | Email Security | High |
| 3 | Enable Safe Links and Safe Attachments with aggressive detonation policies | Email Security | High |
| 4 | Implement URL filtering and proxy controls to block access to known phishing infrastructure | URL Filtering | High |
| 5 | Review and tune email security thresholds based on delivery bypass observed in this campaign | Email Security | High |
| 6 | Deliver targeted phishing awareness content based on the lure theme used in this campaign | Awareness | Medium |
| 7 | Improve user phishing reporting workflow and acknowledgement loop | Reporting | Medium |

---

## Conclusion

**[Closing summary reinforcing key findings, user impact, and remediation status. Suitable for sharing with management alongside the Executive Summary. Address: the phishing subtype and delivery technique, the number of recipients and confirmed interactions, whether account or host compromise occurred, how the campaign was contained, and any outstanding remediation or improvement actions.]**

tasks.title: Validate and classify reported email
tasks.description: Determine whether the reported message is malicious, suspicious, spam, or legitimate. Classify the phishing subtype, such as credential harvesting, malware delivery, business email compromise, callback phishing, QR phishing, or other social engineering.

tasks.title: Preserve phishing evidence
tasks.description: Preserve the original email, headers, body content, embedded URLs, attachments, screenshots, mailbox logs, message trace results, authentication results, and any related user-reported artifacts for investigation and documentation.

tasks.title: Determine campaign scope and affected recipients
tasks.description: Identify all recipients, mailboxes, groups, and external parties that received the message. Determine whether similar messages remain in mailboxes or were delivered elsewhere in the environment.

tasks.title: Analyze headers, sender identity, and delivery path
tasks.description: Analyze the message headers, sender information, authentication results, routing details, reply-to values, lookalike domains, and delivery path to understand how the message was delivered and whether sender identity was spoofed or compromised.

tasks.title: Analyze URLs, domains, and hosted content
tasks.description: Review embedded links, redirect chains, domains, landing pages, host infrastructure, URL shorteners, QR-code targets, and related web content for malicious behavior, credential harvesting, payload delivery, or impersonation.

tasks.title: Analyze attachments and payload behavior
tasks.description: Inspect attachments, archives, embedded documents, scripts, macros, and other payloads for malicious behavior. Determine whether the message delivered malware, droppers, remote access tools, or other suspicious content.

tasks.title: Extract, validate, and track IOCs
tasks.description: Extract and validate indicators of compromise from message content, headers, attachments, hosted infrastructure, and analysis results. Add confirmed indicators to the case and share with downstream systems as authorized.

tasks.title: Determine user interaction and compromise status
tasks.description: Identify whether recipients opened the message, clicked links, submitted credentials, replied, enabled macros, executed attachments, approved MFA prompts, or otherwise interacted with the phishing content. Determine whether user or host compromise occurred.

tasks.title: Contain phishing messages and infrastructure
tasks.description: Remove or quarantine matching messages from mailboxes, block malicious senders, domains, URLs, IPs, and hashes as appropriate, and disable malicious inbox rules or other persistence mechanisms associated with the phishing activity.

tasks.title: Remediate affected accounts and hosts
tasks.description: For impacted users or systems, reset passwords, revoke sessions and tokens, review MFA status, identify malicious inbox rules, investigate suspicious sign-ins, isolate affected hosts if needed, and remove malicious artifacts or persistence.

tasks.title: Notify affected users and stakeholders
tasks.description: Notify impacted recipients, service desk staff, messaging administrators, management, and other stakeholders as appropriate. Provide clear guidance on password resets, MFA review, reporting procedures, host triage, and additional follow-up steps.

tasks.title: Improve detections, blocking, and awareness content
tasks.description: Update email protections, detections, allow and block lists, user guidance, awareness material, and reporting procedures based on the observed phishing technique, lure, and control gaps identified during the investigation.

tasks.title: Document findings and close case
tasks.description: Document the phishing type, delivery mechanism, affected users, compromise status, containment actions, business impact, and lessons learned. Confirm required remediation and notifications are complete before case closure.
